data.name: Khairanah
data.gender_notes: Khairanah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Freshness of the morning dew or anything new and fresh. The name Khairanah carries the meaning “Morning dew or fresh” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khairanah usually hope their child will grow to embody morning dew or fresh and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of the freshness and renewal that comes with each new day
data.etymology: Khairanah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Morning dew or fresh.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khairanah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Khairanah
in_english.long_meaning: Khairanah is derived from the Arabic root 'خَيْر' (khayr), meaning goodness, charity, and abundance. This name signifies a person who embodies kindness, generosity, and benevolence. In Islamic tradition, the term 'khayr' is often used to denote good deeds and charitable actions. The name Khairanah reflects a personality that is compassionate, altruistic, and brings goodness to others.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Khairanah" holds a deep cultural significance in the Islamic world. In Middle Eastern cultures, it is a common name for girls, evoking a sense of new beginnings and freshness. The freshness is a reminder of the beauty and renewal found in nature, which is often seen as a metaphor for the good and pure aspects of life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, "Khairanah" embodies the idea of renewal and rejuvenation. It is a reminder of the importance of starting fresh and seeking the blessings of Allah (SWT) in every moment. In Islamic teachings, the night and day cycle is seen as a metaphor for the passage of time and the opportunity for renewal and growth. The name "Khairanah" can be seen as a reminder of this spiritual truth, encouraging us to approach each day with a fresh and open heart. It is also a reminder of the spiritual renewal that comes from seeking knowledge, performing good deeds, and striving towards closer connection with Allah (SWT).
